chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “May Allah keep you well, what is the easiest thing by which a servant enters the Fire?”
He said: “Whoever consumes a dirham from the wealth of the orphan—and we are the orphan.”

key_terms.أَبِي بَصِيرٍ: Abū Baṣīr, the narrator reporting this hadith
key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, Imam Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Bāqir عليه السلام
key_terms.النَّارَ: the Fire, meaning punishment in the Hereafter
key_terms.الْيَتِيمُ: the orphan; here used in a special referential sense in the Imam’s statement
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a dirham; even a very small amount of wealth
key_terms.مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ: the property of the orphan, whose unlawful consumption is severely condemned

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say is one of the easiest ways for a person to enter the Fire?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that consuming even a small amount from the wealth of the orphan is among the easiest paths to the Fire. In the context of the chapter on khums, the statement “and we are the orphan” indicates the sanctity of the rights connected to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and the grave consequence of violating them.
